Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.
Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Gupta,Acting Chief Justice Hon'ble Kshitij Shailendra,J.
1.

Heard Sri Mukesh Chandra Gupta, learned counsel for the petitioners, learned standing counsel for the State-respondents and Sri Vaibhav Tripathi, learned counsel for National Highway Authority of India.
2. The prayer made in the instant petition is for a direction to respondent nos. 3 & 4 to pay compensation to the petitioners for the acquired land.

3. It appears from the representation annexed with the writ petition that the land over which the petitioners claim title was acquired under the provisions of the National Highway Authority of India Act and notification under Section 3(1)A & 3(1)D have also been made in the newspaper.

sentences.text: It has not been clarified in the writ petition whether any award has been made so far or not.

The only assertion Ramesh Chand And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And 4 Others on 16 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66481950/
1 is that the petitioners have not been paid any compensation.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. Since the acquisition is under the National Highway Act, 1956, the respondents were bound to declare award within time frame stipulated under the Act otherwise the consequences as stipulated would ensue.
5. In such circumstances, no direction is required to be issued.
Moreover, in case award has already been made, it is always open to the petitioners to approach the competent authority with prayer for withdrawal of compensation amount.

6. The petition stands disposed of accordingly.
(Kshitij Shailendra,J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta,ACJ.) Order Date :- 16.12.2023
